The code is in good shape. Three natural improvements remain before the design is complete as a self-contained collection type:

1. **`insert` should return `boolean`** — callers currently have no way to know if a key was actually added (vs. silently ignored as a duplicate); making it return `boolean` is the standard collection contract
2. **`size()` in O(1)** — currently callers must do `tree.inOrder().size()` which allocates a list; a tracked `size` field makes this free
3. **`toString()` override** — `System.out.println(tree)` currently prints a JVM identity hash; overriding it to return the in-order sequence makes the class debuggable

**`insert` returns `boolean`** — a `contains` check gates the actual recursive insert. Duplicates return `false` immediately; new keys insert, increment `size`, and return `true`. This matches the `java.util.Set` contract callers would expect.

**`size()` in O(1)** — a `private int size` field is incremented on every successful insert. No traversal needed.

**`toString()` override** — delegates to `inOrder().toString()`, so `System.out.println(tree)` produces a human-readable sorted sequence rather than a JVM identity hash.
